symbols.name: number of axes
symbols.meaning: The number of cyclic axes in the product ring, a count of axes.
symbols.quote: Let $d$ be the number of axes.

symbols.name: axis length
symbols.meaning: The length of axis $i$, a count of positions on that axis.
symbols.quote: Let $s_i$ be the length of axis $i$, a count of positions on that axis, and assume $s_1,\ldots,s_d$ are pairwise coprime.

symbols.name: total coefficient count
symbols.meaning: The product of the axis lengths, which counts the coefficients of the convolution.
symbols.quote: Let $S=s_1s_2\cdots s_d$ be the total number of coefficients.

symbols.name: ring variable
symbols.meaning: The formal variable of the ring $\mathbb C[x]/(x^S-1)$ on the source side.
symbols.quote: Let $x$ be the variable of the ring $\mathbb C[x]/(x^S-1)$.

symbols.name: prefix length product
symbols.meaning: The product of the axis lengths before axis $i$, which is the integer $s_1\cdots s_{i-1}$.
symbols.quote: Let $P_i=s_1\cdots s_{i-1}$ be the product of the lengths before axis $i$, with $P_1=1$.

symbols.name: inverse multiplier
symbols.meaning: The inverse of $P_i$ modulo $s_i$, an integer with $\mu_iP_i\equiv1\pmod{s_i}$.
symbols.quote: Let $\mu_i$ be the inverse of $P_i$ modulo $s_i$, so that $\mu_iP_i\equiv1\pmod{s_i}$; it exists because $P_i$ is coprime to $s_i$.

symbols.name: axis map
symbols.meaning: The algebra map from the cyclic-convolution ring to the product of cyclic axes.
symbols.quote: Let $\Phi$ be the algebra map sending $x$ to $\prod_i x_i^{\mu_i}$.

symbols.name: coefficient index
symbols.meaning: A coefficient index of the convolution, an integer with $0\le k<S$.
symbols.quote: Let $k$ be a coefficient index with $0\le k<S$.

symbols.name: mixed-radix digit
symbols.meaning: The digit of $k$ on axis $j$ in its mixed-radix expansion, with $0\le a_j<s_j$.
symbols.quote: It has a unique mixed-radix expansion $k=\sum_{j=1}^d a_jP_j$ with $0\le a_j<s_j$, and $a_j$ is the mixed-radix digit of $k$ on axis $j$.

symbols.name: axis coordinate
symbols.meaning: The exponent of $x_i$ in $\Phi(x^k)$, reduced to $0\le b_i<s_i$.
symbols.quote: Let $b_i$ be the exponent of $x_i$ in $\Phi(x^k)$, reduced so that $0\le b_i<s_i$.

relations.quote: The map $\Phi$ is an isomorphism that preserves [cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md), so a product of two lists is computed axis by axis.
